chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Al-Faḍl ibn Yūnus, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام and said: I have female servants with me in Makkah. Should I instruct them to enter iḥrām for hajj on the Day of Tarwiyah, then take them out so they may witness the rites, or should I leave them behind in Makkah?

He said: He عليه السلام said, “If you take them out with you, then that is better; and if you leave them behind with a trustworthy person, then there is no harm. There is no hajj nor ʿumrah upon the owned servant until he or she is freed.”

key_terms.ثِقَةٍ: a trustworthy person with whom they may be left
key_terms.عُمْرَةٌ: the lesser pilgrimage, mentioned here alongside hajj
key_terms.يَوْمَ ٱلتَّرْوِيَةِ: the eighth day of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, when the hajj rites begin
key_terms.يُعْتَقَ: to be freed or emancipated, after which obligation begins
key_terms.ٱلْجَوَارِي: female servants or slave girls in the questioner's care
key_terms.ٱلْحَجِّ: the pilgrimage rites being discussed in terms of participation and obligation
key_terms.ٱلْمَمْلُوكِ: an owned slave, for whom hajj and ʿumrah are not yet obligatory
key_terms.ٱلْمَنَاسِكَ: the ritual acts and ceremonies of hajj

ai.seo_question: Is hajj or ʿumrah obligatory on a slave, and should female servants be taken to the hajj rites?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal ruling regarding enslaved female servants during hajj. The Imam عليه السلام states that taking them along to witness the rites is preferable, but leaving them in Makkah with a trustworthy person is also permitted. He further clarifies that hajj and ʿumrah are not obligatory upon a slave until emancipation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2887 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Fadl ibn Yunus, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (as): "I have female servants with me in Mecca. Should I instruct them to enter into the state of Ihram for Hajj on the Day of Tarwiyah and take them out to witness the rites, or should I leave them behind in Mecca?"

Imam (as) said: "If you take them out with you, that is better. However, if you leave them behind with someone trustworthy, there is no harm in that. There is no obligation of Hajj or 'Umrah on a servant until they are freed."
